description.value: A cross-sectional structural MRI study investigating prefrontal and midsagittal morphological differences in children with PTSD symptoms compared with healthy controls, using volumetric analyses and voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: In this investigation we sought to more specifically localize morphological differences associated with pediatric PTSD beyond the cerebral lobe level by investigating prefrontal cortex and midsagittal structures.

value: We hypothesized that the prefrontal cortex would demonstrate morphological variation in children with PTSD symptoms when compared with healthy controls.

We further hypothesized that voxel-based techniques would help to specify which areas of the prefrontal cortex were most aberrant, such as the orbitofrontal area, the prefrontal region most involved in emotion and affect.
we hypothesized reduced corpus callosum areas in children with PTSD.
we hypothesized volumetric differences between PTSD and controls in this region.
we hypothesized smaller vermis volumes in PTSD patients than in controls.

value: The PTSD group showed significantly greater gray matter volume compared with the control group in a large cluster within the ventral prefrontal regions, with two peaks, one in the right rectal gyrus and the other in the left medial gyrus.
Significantly greater gray matter volume also was observed bilaterally in the occipital lobe. The control group did not show significantly greater gray matter volume than the PTSD group.
Voxel-based analysis further localized increased gray matter density to the ventral prefrontal regions, including the rectal and medial gyri.
